findings.title: Remote Code Execution via SSRF + Eval Injection (Multi-Service Chain)
findings.description:
The flask_app container executes a multi-step chain that allows arbitrary Python eval() injection:
1. /api/set?url= lets an attacker set any URL as the 'script source'
2. The /names endpoint returns the raw stored name value
3. flask_app fetches http://nginx/api/get to get the script URL, then fetches the script, then calls eval(json.loads(script)['script'])
4. By setting name=JSON payload and api_url=http://nginx/names, the attacker controls what Python expression is evaluated

Attack chain:
- GET /name/set?name={"script":"open('/FLAG.txt').read()"}
- GET /api/set?url=http://nginx/names
- GET /app → flask_app fetches http://nginx/names (our JSON), evals open('/FLAG.txt').read()

Hint context: 'The developer was trying to make everything so secure that he ended up making it insecure' - the developer used nginx as a config store thinking it was secure, but the relationships between the name endpoint and the API URL endpoint created an exploit chain.
